submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective detector for the second token of a strongly constraining local bigram: it fires on a token narrowly predicted by the immediately preceding token, covering memorized cross-word chunks (what/What + ’s, What/How + do/does, thou + verb, noun + of as in way/Cuba/Department of, the + Supreme, in + more) and word-internal subword completions (H+es, K+om, S+app, s+elt). Equally frequent but weakly constraining pairs (as + well, What + eat, the + United) do not drive it, so it tracks cue strength, not token frequency.

rival_explanations: Broader unigram reading: it fires on frequent function words and common subword pieces (of, do, ’, more) wherever they appear, regardless of the preceding token — predicts 'of' after 'zebra' or 'do' after 'others' fire, but both measure 0.0.

Narrower wh-question reading: it detects only auxiliaries/contractions completing what/how/who questions — predicts thou + best, noun + of, the + Supreme, in + more, and subword completions stay silent, but the scan and probes show they drive it.

Lookahead reading: it fires on the cue token (What, thou, way) in preparation of the upcoming completion (’s, do, best, of) — predicts peaks before the completion and a coherent Jacobian-promoted upcoming-token set, but peaks sit on the completion itself with single-token replacement of the left cue killing 83-101% of strength, and Jacobian kurtosis is ~3.8 (near-Gaussian, no specific promoted set).

Pikes Peak Branch, National League of American Pen Women, was organized in November 1954, with six Charter Members. These Charter Members were Myrtle Chance Allen, Evelyn Reese Chase, Rae B. Cross, Nell Womack Evans, Bertha O. Klug, Sylvia Pezoldt, Roslee Porter, and Elizabeth Shafer. The Group’s Charter was granted on March 12, 1955.
Throughout the years, this organization of professional creative writers, artists and musicians has grown to a membership between 25 and 35. The NLAPW motto, “One for all and all for one”, is no mere cliché with Pikes Peak Branch members, who share each other’s interests, problems, sales, and triumphs.
This is done on a Branch basis, in smaller workshops, and on a one-to-one basis, with members sharing market tips and news, techniques and helpful criticisms, and sustaining one another through solid and lasting relationships.
Our members are active professional women writers, musicians and artists–in diverse medias; all selling their books, fiction and nonfiction; music, verse and mixed artistic medias to a great variety of national publications. Members are involved in editing, reporting, lecturing, performing, researching, taking photographs, working in advertising and public relations, creating commercial and fine art, holding one-woman juried shows, selling their paintings and sculptures around the country.
Among our members, we have won awards in state, regional, national and international awards for their work in art, music and writing. Many have been listed in several Who’s Who: e.g., Directory of International Biography, International Who’s Who in Poetry, 2,000 Women of Achievements, Who’s Who in the West, Who’s Who in American Women, and Outstanding Young Women of America, to mention a few.
The Branch has also sponsored writers ‘conferences, hosted art shows, juried art and poetry contests, events to encourage and support young women in the arts and other opportunities such as the annual Member Art Show. Currently, the Pikes Peak Branch sponsors three outreach programs locally-The Poetry in the Schools Project, Musical Instruments in the Schools and their annual elementary school ‘Bucks for Books Drive’ in collaboration with the local chapter of DAR. The Flash Fiction Contest brings the Branch recognition nationally and internationally annually. Their vision continues to provide support to all Branch members, and further seek ways to put the National League of American Pen Women in the public eye.
Currently, the members and friends of Pikes Peak Pen Women meet for lunch and a program the second Saturday of each month, from 11:00–1:30. Traditionally, in earlier years, a new member received a bracelet and an insignia charm. The expense and the demise of the popularity of the dangle bracelet has allowed that tradition to die. A systematic review of allostatic load in relation to socioeconomic position: Poor fidelity and major inconsistencies in biomarkers employed.
The association between disease and socioeconomic position (SEP) is well established. Allostatic load (AL), or physiological 'wear and tear', is a concept that aims to elucidate the biological consequences of stress that may underlie these associations. The primary objective of this paper is to review the biomarkers and methods used to operationalise the concept of AL in studies analysing the association between AL and SEP. Four databases (Embase, Global Health, MEDLINE, and PsychINFO) were searched using terms related to AL, biomarkers and SEP. Data extraction focused on the methods used to calculate AL indices. The frequency of pair-wise combinations of biomarkers were used to assess the level of overlap in AL definition between studies. Twenty-six studies analysing the association between AL and SEP were included. There was no consistent method of operationalizing AL across studies. Individual biomarkers and biological systems included in the AL index differed widely across studies, as did the method of calculating the AL index. All studies included at least one cardiovascular- and metabolic-related biomarker in AL indices, while only half of studies included at least one hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis biomarker and approximately one third an immune response-related biomarker. All but three studies found evidence of an association between lower SEP and higher AL. Many studies lacked fidelity to the original concept of AL in which stress was considered central. The considerable variation in biomarkers used makes studies in this review difficult to compare. A more critical approach should be taken in the calculation of AL indices in particular to how far it captures the biological effects of psychosocial stress that may underlie socioeconomic differences in health.

كس بلانك للفيزياء النووية. سُمّي المبنى الرئيسي فيه لاحقًا بمختبر بوته.

التعليم 

ولد بوته لوالديه فريدريش بوته وشارلوت هارتونج. من عام 1908 إلى عام 1912، درس بوته في جامعة فريدريش فيلهيلمز (تُسمى اليوم جامعة هومبولت في برلين). في عام 1913، كان مساعد مدرس لماكس بلانك. حصل على الدكتوراه تحت إشراف بلانك في عام 1914.

السنوات المبكرة

عند عودته من روسيا، واصل بوته عمله في بّي تي آر تحت إشراف هانز غايغر في مختبر النشاط الإشعاعي هناك. في عام 1924، نشر بوته فيما يخص طريقته للصدفة. ثم وفي السنوات التالية، طبق هذه الطريقة على الدراسة التجريبية للتفاعلات النووية وتأثير كومبتون وازدواجية موجة الجسيمات للضوء. وبفضل طريقته وتطبيقاتها حصل بوته على جائزة نوبل في الفيزياء عام 1954.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps 'best' as an adjective after 'simple' rather than as a verb completing 'thou', changing its syntactic role.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses the hypothesis's own named weak pair What+eats, keeping the wh-cue but swapping in an unpredictable lexical verb.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses the hypothesis's own named weak pair the+United, keeping 'the' but swapping in an unpredictable completion.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the What cue in the sentence but makes 'do' adjacent to 'they', breaking the local constraining bigram.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The garden with roses and tulips reminded her of childhood summers near the lake.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Places 'of' after the pronoun 'her', a frequent but weakly constraining left context, instead of a selecting noun.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They promised to do better work after the disappointing review last month.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests infinitive 'to do', where 'to' predicts many verbs and constrains 'do' only weakly despite high frequency.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Whenever the old engine stalls, it does restart after a few loud clicks.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Places auxiliary 'does' after generic 'it', a frequent but weakly constraining bigram compared with What/How+does.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The visiting doctors’ lounge was repainted bright white last spring.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the apostrophe in a plural possessive after 'doctors', sharing the delimiter without the constraining What cue.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He predicted storms and floods, wanting more funding for coastal defences.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Places 'more' after the weak verb 'wanting' rather than a constraining cue such as 'once' or 'nothing'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She cleared the wooden breakfast table of dishes before the guests arrived.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Places 'of' after the concrete noun 'table', which barely constrains it, unlike selecting nouns such as Kingdom.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Tell me, thou slow traveller, where have you rested on your long journey?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the archaic cue 'thou' but follows it with an adjective phrase, so the lookahead rival fires while the bigram claim stays silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They found their way back through the dark forest long after midnight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the cue word 'way' after a generic possessive so the lookahead rival predicts firing but no constraining bigram completes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She admired teh Supreme court ruling with great interest yesterday morning.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Corrupted prompt: misspells the cue as 'teh' before 'Supreme', altering the constraining left token while keeping the peak.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Corrupted prompt: misspells the cue as 'Waht' before 'do', testing whether the exact constraining bigram is required.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: You will never guess what’s hidden inside the old wooden chest upstairs.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout paraphrasing the What+'s chunk in a novel guessing-game context absent from the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: How does a submarine navigate beneath the thick polar ice cap?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout with a novel How+does bigram in a submarine genre far from the wh-question examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Who does the night shift at the small harbour clinic nowadays?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout extending the wh+auxiliary class to the novel cue 'Who' with the claimed token 'does'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: For thou art no longer welcome beyond these ancient stones tonight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout with a novel thou+verb bigram ('thou art') as a single completion token, contra the narrow wh rival.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The ancient Kingdom of Kush traded gold along the great wide river.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout with the novel noun+of chunk 'Kingdom of' in an ancient-history context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She filed the complaint with the Ministry of Health early last spring.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout with the novel institutional noun+of chunk 'Ministry of' in a bureaucratic context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He studied the tactics of Alexander the Great during his history course.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout with the novel epithet bigram 'the Great', testing the the+X class beyond 'the Supreme'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After the storm they wanted nothing more than a hot meal and rest.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout with the novel constraining cue 'nothing' before 'more' in an idiomatic than-complement.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: From Homer, Herodotus, Thucydides and Xenophon come tales of ancient wars.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout paralleling H+esiod with a novel H+erodotus subword completion in a classics list.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The choir sang the chorus once more for the delighted evening crowd.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout with the novel constraining cue 'once' before 'more' in a concert-encore context.
